Diana —

Thanks for the note and the questionnaire. High level answers first, then proposed next steps:

1) Legal-hold / freeze: Redwood supports administrative legal holds at the tenant level. When a hold is requested we snapshot the operator/admin activity ledger and mark the corresponding buckets as immutable. Typical time-to-freeze is sub-2 hours for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we coordinate an on-prem maintenance window but can confirm immutability within 8 hours. We also record a signed manifest (HMAC) at freeze time.

2) Ad-hoc retrieval SLA and formats: We can provide on-demand exports in CSV/NDJSON and signed tarball (gzip) with a manifest and checksums. Standard SLA for hosted customers: 48 business hours for full retention-range exports up to 90 days; 5-7 business days for historic exports beyond 90 days (larger bundles). For Dedicated/Private customers we can negotiate faster windows in the contract. Timestamps are ISO-8601 with TZ and we preserve the original event timestamp and a server-ingest timestamp when available.

3) Chain-of-custody and attestation: We attach a chain_of_custody_manifest_template.csv (sample) that lists export start/end, checksums, HMAC signatures, and operator IDs. We also include a signed statement when exports are attested for audits.

Next steps I propose:
- I attached our quick playbook (redwood-log-retrieval-playbook-v1.pdf) which maps request types to SLAs/format and includes sample manifests.
- Kimberley/Marissa: can you review the attached playbook and confirm we can commit to the 48 business-hour SLA for hosted exports for Elderwood?
- Diana: if that works, we can run an on-demand export test (small window) this week and provide result files and checksums for you to validate timestamp fidelity.

Attachments: redwood-log-retrieval-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB); chain_of_custody_manifest_template.csv (CSV, 2KB)

Avery / Diana — quick clarifications from a security/compliance perspective:

- Retention/immutability: for hosted customers we maintain a rolling immutable snapshot for 365 days by default; retention beyond that is configured per-account. Legal-hold overrides retention garbage collection immediately and we escalate to the export team to create attestable snapshots.

- Timestamp fidelity: events have two timestamps: event_time (client/system time) and redwood_ingest_time. Both are included in exports; we canonicalize output to UTC in the manifest but preserve original timezone values in the event payload.

- Export sampling and PII: we can provide full exports or scoped slices (tenant-only, user-id, timeframe). If the SIG requires sampled evidence instead of full exports, we will document sampling methodology in the manifest (sampling seed, deterministic hash).

- Chain-of-custody: we require a two-person review for attestation (engineer + security reviewer). The manifest includes revision history and a SHA256 digest for each file.

Marissa — please confirm legal is OK with committing the 48 business-hour hosted SLA for ad-hoc exports. If so, I will add the attestation step and the 2-person review to the playbook and sign-off matrix.

— Kimberly Park
